# CBDB-Desktop: Association Pairs revisions, 2026-10-12

Found while writing the Association Pairs section of the user's guide, not from an automated-testing report, so these entries have no CBDB-D numbers yet. Assign numbers as needed. ASP-1 and ASP-2 are in the 2026-10-10 report. All changes are in Code/assocpairs_form_backend.go and the form's index.html. They were compiled and checked with test queries.

## Summary

| Ref | Issue | Fix | Status |

| ASP-3 | Source titles, literary genre, occasion, topic and institution names were always blank | Wrong column name corrected; enrichment UPDATEs now log errors | Compiled, tested |
| ASP-4 | KinChn held the kin person's Chinese name, not the relationship; kin name and Chinese relationship were not returned | Network record and read-back now return name and relationship separately, in both languages | Compiled, tested |

| ASP-8 | Associations with no kin intermediary or no claimer showed [Unknown] as the kin, association-kin or claimer name and relationship | Lookups now run only when the ID or code is greater than 0 | Compiled, tested |

## ASP-3: Lookup descriptions always blank

**Symptom.** In the Social Network results, Source and 書名 were blank on every row, although c_source held valid IDs that exist in TEXT_CODES. Running the source-title assignment by itself in DB Browser worked.

**Cause.** One UPDATE in handleQuery fills ten lookup fields: literary genre, occasion, topic, institution and source title, each in English and Chinese. One assignment referred to LITERARYGENRE_CODES.c_lit_genre_chn, but the column is c_lit_genre_desc_chn. SQLite checks every column before running a statement, so the whole UPDATE failed with "no such column". The error was discarded, because the statement was run as a bare tx.Exec(...), so nothing was logged. All ten fields stayed blank in every query. The codes themselves were correct, so the Neo4j code files (LitGenreCodes, OccasionCodes, TopicCodes, InstitutionCodes) contained codes with empty descriptions.

**Fix.** The column name was corrected. All four enrichment UPDATEs on ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR now check the error and log it with a message identifying which statement failed.

## ASP-4: Kin fields mislabelled

**Symptom.** Found by code review. readSocialNetwork read c_kin_desc and c_kin_chn into KinDesc and KinChn. But c_kin_chn holds the kin person's Chinese **name**; the Chinese relationship is in c_kin_desc_chn. The KinChn column in Export Query Results therefore held a name, and the kin person's English name was not returned at all.

**Fix.** The kin group of AssocPairsNetworkRecord is now KinID, KinCode, KinName, KinChn (name), KinDesc, KinDescChn (relationship). The SELECT and Scan in readSocialNetwork and the Export Query Results columns were updated to match.

## ASP-5: Association-kin fields never filled

**Symptom.** Found by code review. c_assoc_kin_id and c_assoc_kin_code are copied from ASSOC_DATA, but nothing filled c_assoc_kin_name, c_assoc_kin_chn, c_assoc_kin_desc or c_assoc_kin_desc_chn, so AssocKinDesc and AssocKinChn were always blank.

**Fix.** Four lookups (BIOG_MAIN for the name, KINSHIP_CODES for the relationship) were added to the kin/claimer enrichment UPDATE. The association-kin group of the record now matches the kin group: AssocKinID, AssocKinCode, AssocKinName, AssocKinChn, AssocKinDesc, AssocKinDescChn. The read-back and the results export were updated to match.

## ASP-6: Distance between the two people

**Issue.** ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR.c_distance is meant to hold the great-circle distance between the two people's index addresses, from ZZZ_DISTANCE_DATA (keyed on c_personid, c_assoc_id). Nothing filled it, and it was not returned to the page.

**Fix.**

- A new UPDATE, run after the other enrichment steps, looks the pair up in both directions, because the table may store only one ordering of each pair:

```
UPDATE ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR SET c_distance = COALESCE(
  (SELECT d.c_distance FROM ZZZ_DISTANCE_DATA d
    WHERE d.c_personid = ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR.c_person_id AND d.c_assoc_id = ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR.c_node_id),
  (SELECT d.c_distance FROM ZZZ_DISTANCE_DATA d
    WHERE d.c_personid = ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR.c_node_id AND d.c_assoc_id = ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR.c_person_id))
```

Both lookups use the existing index ZZZ_DISTANCE_DATA_pair. The update covers association and kinship edges.

- AssocPairsNetworkRecord has a new field, Distance \*float64 (JSON distance). It is a pointer so that a missing distance comes through as NULL / null rather than 0, which would look like two people at the same place.
- Export Query Results has a new Distance column, written at full precision by a new helper, fmtOptFloat, and blank when unknown.
- The Social Network table has a new Distance column, shown to two decimals by a new helper, nd(). Unknown distances are blank and sort to the end.

**For the user's guide.** ZZZ_DISTANCE_DATA only has rows for pairs where both people have an index address, so a blank Distance means that one or both people lack an index address. Distance is measured between index addresses (usually county or prefecture seats), not between the places where the association took place.

## ASP-7: Dist column blank in the Social Network table

**Symptom.** The Dist column was always blank, and sorting on it did nothing.

**Cause.** renderNetworkTable read r.dist and sorted on 'dist', but the server sends the field as nodeDist.

**Fix.** The cell, the sort key and the numeric-sort set (renamed nullableNumCols, now also containing distance) use nodeDist.

## ASP-8: [Unknown] shown for absent kin and claimers

**Symptom.** Once ASP-4 and ASP-5 filled in the kin and association-kin fields, every association without a kin intermediary showed [Unknown] as the kin name and relationship. The same happened for the association-kin and claimer fields.

**Cause.** c_kin_id, c_kin_code, c_assoc_kin_id and c_assoc_kin_code are part of the primary key of ASSOC_DATA, so they cannot be NULL. When no kin is involved, they hold 0. BIOG_MAIN and KINSHIP_CODES both have a 0 row meaning [Unknown], so the lookups found it. c_assoc_claimer_id is written as COALESCE(ad.c_assoc_claimer_id, 0) by the association INSERT, so an association with no claimer behaved the same way.

**Fix.** Each assignment in the kin/claimer enrichment UPDATE is wrapped in a guard on its own key, for example:

```
c_kin_name = CASE WHEN c_kin_id > 0
  THEN (SELECT c_name FROM BIOG_MAIN WHERE c_personid = ZZ_SN_ASSOC_PAIR.c_kin_id) END
```

Names are guarded on the person ID (c_kin_id, c_assoc_kin_id, c_assoc_claimer_id), and relationships on the kinship code (c_kin_code, c_assoc_kin_code). When the key is 0, the field stays NULL and appears blank in the table and the results export.

**Not changed.** The IDs and codes themselves still come through as 0 in Export Query Results and in the Neo4j AssociationRecords file, matching ASSOC_DATA. Only the descriptive fields are left blank. Kinship edges (link type K) are unaffected, because their kin columns are NULL and the guards skip them.

## Not affected

- The GIS, Neo4j, Pajek, Gephi and UCINet exports use only IDs, codes and node distance, so the struct changes do not affect them. They post the network array back, and it decodes into the revised struct unchanged. ASP-3 does improve the Neo4j code files, which now have descriptions.
- No schema changes were needed. Every column used already exists in both ensureAppTables and cbdb.db.schema.sql.
